I've already submitted a bunch of applications, mostly for software engineering or data engineering intern-to-full-time conversion roles. It was a valuable experience where I saw how a real development team operates, plans sprints, manages code reviews, and handles feature rollouts to actual paying clients. By the end of that internship, I felt more confident in my skills, and I think that will help me stand out when I interview.

I need to consider practicalities like health insurance, paying rent, and saving up. A full-time engineering position usually comes with a decent salary, which could help me knock out that debt faster. If I went straight into grad school, funding can be complicated, with some PhD programs offering stipends and others not. Master's programs often require tuition payments, and scholarships can be competitive. I'm thinking that a good job in industry could serve a dual purpose: alleviating financial strain and giving me career momentum. It would allow me to figure out if I truly want to go back to school.
